title: Close the Review Loop
objective: Respond to review on the real contribution: address each comment with a follow-up commit or a written no-change reason, using a maintainer review if one exists or a documented self-review plus a second-person review if none has arrived.
whyThisMatters: Opening a pull request is the start of collaboration. The skill maintainers actually need is a visible response to each comment without rewriting history they cannot follow.
evidence: The pull-request URL from os1t1-003 (upstream or public fork)
Review thread URL(s), or a committed self-review dated in the note plus the second-person reviewer's name or handle and date
A table with one row per review item: comment summary, reply, and either a follow-up commit SHA or the phrase no change plus a one-sentence reason
Git log showing a commit timestamp after the first review comment or after the self-review date, unless every row is no change
Reflection notes answering the task questions
AI disclosure entry when AI materially influenced the work
acceptanceCriteria: The table has one row for every review comment on the pull request, or — if no maintainer review exists — at least four self-review items plus every item the second-person reviewer raised.
Each row contains a comment summary, a reply that names the file or line under discussion, and either a commit SHA or the exact phrase "no change" plus a one-sentence reason.
At least one commit on the branch has an author date after the first review comment (or after the recorded self-review date), unless every row is marked no change.
The pull-request description still contains the upstream issue URL from os1t1-003.
Every reply is written as one or more complete sentences; no reply is only an emoji, only "fixed", or only a pasted patch with no explanation.
